title: Executive Officer (EO), moving up from Administrative Officer
summary: Moving from AO to EO: running a caseload or small area of work with more independence, and often guiding or supervising others. Promotion is normally by applying for a vacancy and being assessed on merit, so the aim is to build the skills and the examples that show you are already working at the next grade.

areas.label: Behaviours and evidence at EO level
areas.why: Show the next grade's Behaviours with real examples from your current job.

areas.label: Core office skills at a higher level
areas.why: Plain English, emails, spreadsheets and handling information are expected to be strong at EO.

areas.label: Written and spoken communication
areas.why: Briefing, replying to complex enquiries and explaining decisions clearly.

areas.label: Rules, fairness and governance
areas.why: Apply the rules to less routine cases and explain why they exist.

areas.label: Guiding and supervising others
areas.why: Allocating work, giving feedback and helping a new starter.

stages.label: Understand the next grade
stages.blurb: Read the EO role profile and talk to your manager about what is expected.

stages.label: Build the skills and evidence
stages.blurb: Strengthen the skills and gather examples at EO level.

stages.label: Show it and apply
stages.blurb: Use the examples in applications and interviews, and take on EO-level tasks.

actions.label: Read an EO job advert and its role profile from start to finish
actions.detail: Use Civil Service Jobs, or your department's internal vacancies, to read what EO roles ask for. Note which Behaviours and which tasks you already do.

actions.label: Talk to your line manager about promotion
actions.detail: Ask what evidence they would want to see, and whether there are acting-up or temporary promotion opportunities in your team.

actions.label: Keep a log of examples that show EO-level work
actions.detail: Write each example as situation, task, action and result, using I and giving numbers. Aim for six, one per Behaviour that appears in EO adverts.

actions.label: Take on one task that stretches you
actions.detail: Offer to cover a colleague's duties, train a new starter or lead a small improvement, so you have a real example at the next grade.

actions.label: Practise an interview out loud
actions.detail: Ask a colleague to put three Behaviour questions to you and check each answer has a clear result.

apply.label: Apply for EO vacancies
apply.detail: Apply to EO vacancies as they appear, in your own department and across the Civil Service. Promotion normally follows fair and open competition on merit, so you can apply before you feel completely ready: each application, and its feedback, is practice.
